subject: Post-call: evidence request & network boundary snapshot for private deploy
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@clearwavehealth.com>, Eric Morales <eric.morales@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: evidence request & network boundary snapshot for private deploy

Hi Anita / Eric —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the clarity on the clinical PII flows and the constraints around air-gapped evaluation. Per our discussion I wanted to capture the immediate asks and next steps so your security and infra teams have a single reference: 

1) Network boundary snapshot: can you share the (1) internal subnet topology for the pilot environment, (2) any egress proxy/NGFW IP ranges, and (3) the list of external hosts you allow outbound (we can accept a CSV).

2) PII classification and retention: you mentioned all raw PHI will be stripped before being stored outside your VPC for the pilot, and minimal hashed ids are acceptable for observability. Please confirm required retention (logs/objects) for 90 / 180 / 365 day options and whether deletion APIs are required.

3) Audit & logging evidence: your SOC/infosec team asked for example logging artifacts (audit log format, retention policy, sample events) — I'm attaching a short sample (audit-logging-sample.txt) and a simple dataflow template (redwood-private-dataflow-template.xlsx) to help map fields.

4) Egress allowlist & approval path: we will provide a recommended egress-IP list for our Private runtime. Please confirm whether you need per-IP approvals or CIDR ranges; also clarify the procurement lead for firewall changes (procurement@clearwavehealth.com?)

Next steps (proposed):
- You share network snapshot + retention target by EOD Wednesday (5/19)
- We provide an egress IP CSV and a short checklist for on-prem/air-gapped acceptance (ETA: 5/18)
- Joint working call with infra (30m) once artifacts are exchanged (proposed 5/20)

Attaching: redwood-private-dataflow-template.xlsx (mapping), audit-logging-sample.txt (sample events). I’ll follow up with the egress list tomorrow morning.

If anything above is incorrect or I missed a requirement, flag and I’ll update.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachment stubs: redwood-private-dataflow-template.xlsx (xlsx), audit-logging-sample.txt (text)
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@clearwavehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Eric Morales <eric.morales@clearwavehealth.com>, procurement@clearwavehealth.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: evidence request & network boundary snapshot for private deploy

Karthik — thanks for the recap and the artifacts. Quick answers inline: 

1) Network snapshot: we can export a simple topology but need to redact internal hostnames. We’ll provide: VPC CIDRs, subnet names and purposes (compute, mgmt, bastion), and the NGFW egress proxy IPs.

2) Retention: default retention is 365 days for audit logs; for the pilot we can accept 90 days for forensic logs if we receive proof deletion is automated. For PII (patient identifiers) retention inside the pilot environment must be limited to 30 days unless otherwise approved.

3) Audit evidence: please provide sample event schema and an example of an immutable audit trail (write-once log export or signed event). We require the ability to ingest logs into our Splunk indexer; provide a sample syslog or S3 export layout.

4) Egress approvals: procurement manages firewall change requests but security signs off. Please send the egress IPs and our procurement team will review timing.

We will upload the network snapshot to a shared Drive folder (link below) and redact as necessary.

Blocking items for procurement/security before can move to pilot: 
- Signed data processing addendum (DPA) with subprocessor list (we’ll need that attached to the purchase order)
- Evidence of audit log immutability and retention controls
- Clear egress allowlist and rollback plan for firewall changes

I’ve looped Eric (infra) and procurement for timelines. We’ll aim to deliver a redacted topology + retention confirmation by 5/19 EOD.

Thanks,
Anita Shah
Director, Information Security | ClearWave Health
anita.shah@clearwavehealth.com

On the attachments you sent: the template looks helpful — once we have your sample syslog export we can map fields to our Splunk ingest.

Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFGH-example

-----Original message-----
(quoted for context)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: evidence request & network boundary snapshot for private deploy

Hi Anita — thanks for the clarity and timeline. A few operational notes from our side: 

- Egress IPs: we’ll send a CIDR-first recommendation plus CIDR-to-IP expanded list. For air-gapped installs we can provide an appliance-based package with no external egress; for VPC-based private deployments the runtime needs outbound access to pull model weights in the initial bootstrap and for updates (we can pre-stage weights in your S3 if preferred).

- Audit trail: attached is a small sample log export (audit-logging-sample.txt) with typical event ids and timestamping. We write structured JSON events and can export to S3 with object immutability (via S3 Object Lock) or stream to your syslog.

- Retention: our platform supports retention controls per-log-bucket and we can configure automatic lifecycle policies to expire objects after the agreed window; we will include a deletion API for removal on request.

Attaching the network egress CSV (network-egress-ip-list.csv) and a short one-pager for the on-prem acceptance checklist. Let me know whether procurement needs a formal change control doc for firewall windows.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: network-egress-ip-list.csv (csv), onprem-acceptance-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Folks — quick follow-up from infra: a few specific asks to make mapping easier: 

- Can Redwood provide a sample of the exact syslog JSON field names you emit (timestamp, event_type, user_id, request_id, model_id, input_hash, output_hash, action) so we can create a Splunk sourcetype mapping?
- For S3 export, we prefer newline-delimited JSON compressed with gzip and stored in a dedicated bucket with Object Lock enabled. If you support multipart uploads and server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) that would be preferred.
- For the bootstrapping flow: confirm whether pre-staging models in our S3 avoids outbound internet calls from the VPC during initial pull. If not, describe the handshake/egress pattern.

If Redwood can provide the sample field mapping + short description of the bootstrap handshake by EOD 5/18 we’ll be able to move procurement to draft the PO.

— Eric
Eric Morales
Principal Cloud Engineer | ClearWave Health

Eric / Anita — good morning. Quick package to close the asks you listed: 

1) Syslog field mapping: attached is a short snippet (we also pasted below) showing the JSON keys we emit: timestamp, level, event_id, actor_id, request_id, model_key, input_hash, output_hash, action, outcome, ctx.remote_addr. We will provide a gzipped NDJSON export to your S3 bucket with SSE-KMS and Object Lock enabled.

2) Bootstrap model pull: if you pre-stage the model weights in your S3 bucket and provide an IAM role (read-only) to the Redwood runtime, no external egress is required for the initial load. Alternately, we support a secure signed-provider handshake that pulls from our shard endpoints — that flow uses outbound HTTPS to 34.83.21.97:443 (we supplied the CIDR/CNAME below).

3) Retention & deletion API: we support lifecycle policies and a deletion API for immediate removal — we’ll include a signed webhook for automation. For the pilot we suggest 90-day forensic retention + 30-day PII retention inside the VPC, matching your guidance; we can update for 365 if security requires.

4) Artifacts uploaded: network snapshot (redacted), syslog-sample.gz (S3-presigned link), and the DPA template. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFGH-example

Next operational steps: 
- We’ll send the CIDR-first egress list (full CSV attached) by noon today.
- If acceptable, schedule a 30-minute runbook review on 5/20 at 10:00 AM PT. We’ll create a short meeting invite and include our infra engineering lead.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Platform Security Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
